source.filename: 2025-A new mechanical model of short wire ropes Theory and experimental.pdf

constitutive_assumptions: Infinitesimal deformation theory with equilibrium equations enforced in the initial reference configuration (linearized regime).
Individual wires behave as shear-deformable curvilinear beams with circular cross-sections according to Saint-Venant theory extended to curved rods.
Cross-section rotations of individual wires coincide with the cross-section rotation of the wire rope.
Constituent wires have linear elastic isotropic material behavior defined by Young's modulus E and shear modulus G.
Limiting assumption that all wires across the rope cross-section simultaneously occupy the same stick-slip state.
In the perfect stick state (S1), eigenstrains are zero and classical monolithic beam kinematics apply.
In the partial stick state (S2), wire eigenstrains cancel wire elongation induced by beam bending curvature while allowing tangential sliding.
In the full slip state (S3), wire eigenstrains eliminate contributions of beam curvature to both wire elongation and wire shear strains, treating wires as independently bending.
In the axial-torsional state (S4), wire eigenstrains cancel the transverse shear strains of the wires.
The rope constitutive stiffness matrix is independent of the axial coordinate s when all wires share the same stick-slip regime.
control_variables: Prescribed loading frequency of 0.2 Hz to enforce quasi-static loading conditions.
14 loading-unloading cycles per displacement test, evaluating the 7th cycle to avoid initial wire settling effects.
Wire material properties (AISI 304 stainless steel with Young's modulus E = 200 GPa and Poisson's ratio nu = 0.3).
Free horizontal sliding of one clamped end to eliminate axial stretching forces and isolate pure flexural response.
dependent_variables: Transverse restoring force / end shear force (F2 or Q2).
Minimum bending stiffness (k_min) fitted along the linear loading branch.
Maximum bending stiffness (k_max) fitted at the onset of the unloading branch.
Axial stiffness (N / epsilon) and reactive torque-to-axial force ratio (T / N) under axial-torsional loading.

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: A Timoshenko shear-deformable beam model incorporating incompatible eigenstrains predicts the upper and lower bounds of bending stiffness in short single- and multi-strand wire ropes.

Classical beam theory assuming perfect stick between wires overestimates maximum bending stiffness by roughly an order of magnitude due to unavoidable interwire sliding at small flexural deformations.

Assuming a partial stick state via eigenstrains (where bending curvature induces no axial elongation in the wires) accurately predicts the experimental maximum bending stiffness with errors between 7% and 32%.

Assuming a full slip state via eigenstrains (where beam curvature contributes neither elongation nor shear strains to wires) predicts the experimental minimum bending stiffness with errors between 1% and 37%.
Accounting for relative wire slip leads to a positive-definite but non-symmetric 6x6 constitutive stiffness matrix that couples bending with shear in addition to axial-torsional coupling.

When wire rope length is shorter than the lay pitch of the lateral strands (e.g., length of 5 cm versus pitch of 7 cm in R2), boundary and torsional effects become pronounced, increasing divergence from uniform 1D beam theory.

The eigenstrain formulation accurately predicts axial-torsional response without parameter calibration, achieving relative errors under 4% for fixed-end and free-end axial stiffness and reactive torque.

experimental_setup: Universal testing machine (MTS 810) configured with a custom pure bending fixture for short wire ropes.
Two rigid arms with two-plate steel clamps and cylindrical housings tightened by four bolts to secure the rope ends.
Left arm anchored rigidly to the MTS 810 load cell to measure total restoring shear force.
Right arm attached to the machine actuator piston via a bottom plate equipped with a low-friction horizontal slider to accommodate end shortening and prevent tension.
Displacement-controlled quasi-static cyclic tests at 0.2 Hz across various amplitudes and rope lengths for single-strand (R1) and seven-strand (R2) ropes.
Tension-torsional testing machine (reported from literature by Utting and Jones 1987) applying prescribed axial elongation under fixed-rotation and free-rotation boundary conditions.
future_work: Extending the mechanical formulation to predict the complete nonlinear hysteresis cycles and energy dissipation loops.
Developing models capable of handling coupled simultaneous bending and tensile loadings.
Investigating non-uniform sliding regimes where individual wires across the cross-section occupy different stick-slip states.
independent_variables: Wire rope architecture (single-strand R1 with 1+6+12+18+24 wires vs. multi-strand R2 with 1+6 strands of 1+6+12 wires each).
Wire rope length L (10, 12, 15, and 20 cm for R1; 5, 7.5, 10, and 12 cm for R2).
Prescribed transverse displacement amplitude (2 to 50 mm for R1; 2.5 to 35 mm for R2).
Boundary condition type (pure transverse displacement with fixed end rotations; fixed vs. free end rotation in axial-torsional tests).
Assumed stick-slip kinematic state (perfect stick S1, partial stick S2, full slip S3, axial-torsional S4).
limitations_inferred: Local contact stress distributions, cross-sectional distortion, and interwire contact pressures are not solved explicitly, relying instead on idealized cross-section-wide eigenstrain kinematic states.
Progressive wire-by-wire slip transitions (e.g., slipping initiating in outer layers before inner layers) are not resolved.
Environmental and tribological parameters such as lubrication, surface roughness, temperature, and wear are not explicitly accounted for.
limitations_stated_by_authors: The upper and lower bounds of bending stiffness are evaluated under the limiting hypothesis that all wires simultaneously undergo the exact same stick-slip sliding regime.
The formulation is restricted to the linear elastic regime and does not predict the force-displacement hysteresis loop shape or damping dissipation.
The current model does not account for coupled bending and tension loading programs.

For very short rope lengths where the lateral strand pitch exceeds the total rope length (e.g., L = 5 cm for R2), boundary and torsional effects become significant and the model is less representative.
Equilibrium equations are enforced in the undeformed configuration (infinitesimal deformation theory), even though specimens experimentally experienced moderately large curvatures.
Precision of clamping devices and degree of clamping tightness introduce experimental boundary uncertainties that may alter effective specimen length.
main_results: The full slip eigenstrain state (S3) accurately predicts the lower bound (minimum stiffness k_min) across all tested lengths with relative errors between 1.0% and 37.0%, aligning with the Foti-Martinelli model.

The partial stick eigenstrain state (S2) accurately captures the upper bound (maximum stiffness k_max) with relative errors between 7.2% and 31.9%, aligning near the lower bound of the experimental confidence region.
The classical beam theory / perfect stick assumption (S1) overestimates maximum bending stiffness by approximately an order of magnitude compared to experimental measurements.
A reduction in maximum bending moment of approximately 73% occurs between the partial stick and full slip conditions for a 10 cm single-strand rope subjected to 5 mm transverse displacement.

The model analytically captures axial-torsional coupling without empirical parameter calibration, yielding 2.3% error on fixed-end axial stiffness, 2.6% error on reactive torque ratio, and 4.0% error on free-end axial stiffness.
The derived 6x6 stiffness matrix exhibits coupling between bending and shear (k25, k36, k52, k63) and is non-symmetric (k_ij != k_ji) in sliding regimes.
modeling_methods: One-dimensional shear-deformable beam theory (Timoshenko beam model) for the overall wire rope.
Saint-Venant beam theory extended to curvilinear thin rods with circular cross-sections for individual constituent wires.
Parametric analytical geometric modeling of helical wires and superhelical (doubly-twisted) wires using Frenet-Serret frames.
Incompatible eigenstrain formulation incorporated into individual wire strain measures to represent interwire stick-slip sliding modes.
Analytical closed-form solution of Dirichlet boundary value problems for pure bending and axial-torsional loading.
Derivation of a 6x6 generalized cross-sectional constitutive stiffness matrix relating stress resultants to beam generalized strains.
performance_metrics: Effective bending stiffness k = F2 / u2 (in kN/mm).
Relative percentage error err(%) = |k_exp - k_the| / k_exp * 100.
Axial-torsional coupling ratio T / N (in mm).
Experimental mean (mu) and standard deviation (sigma) confidence intervals for stiffness.
possible_gap_implications: The calibration-free analytical prediction of lower and upper bounding stiffnesses could aid the structural design of tendon-driven continuum robot backbones, flexible catheter shafts, or variable-stiffness segments utilizing wire ropes by providing rapid bounds on flexural compliance without heavy FE contact simulations.

Because the model only provides lower and upper bounds in the linear regime, employing it in real-time control or shape reconstruction of continuum robots would require extending it to predict full hysteretic damping and coupled tension-bending kinematics.
paper.research_objective: To formulate and validate an analytical 1D shear-deformable beam model using eigenstrains that provides robust, parameter-calibration-free predictions of the minimum and maximum bending stiffnesses (associated with full slip and partial stick states) as well as axial-torsional stiffness for short single-strand and multi-strand wire ropes.
paper.research_problem: Accurately estimating the upper and lower bounds of bending stiffness across hysteresis cycles for short wire ropes without relying on case-by-case empirical parameter fitting or computationally demanding 3D finite element contact models prone to severe convergence issues, overcoming classical beam theory's order-of-magnitude overestimation of maximum bending stiffness.
stiffness_mechanism: interwire stick-slip (perfect stick, partial stick, and full slip states)
internal frictional forces at wire contact interfaces
helical and superhelical wire geometry (pitch, helix radius, lay orientation)
shear deformability of constituent curvilinear wires
paper.title: A new mechanical model of short wire ropes: Theory and experimental validation
